title: Fair and efficient division
description: Allocations of indivisible goods that are envy-free and Pareto-efficient; existence is Sigma-2-complete even for additive values (de Keijzer, Bouveret, Klos and Zhang). The abstraction guesses an envy-free allocation and the check one that dominates it. Being dominated depends on sums, which a clause cannot say, so the refinement is a rule (Shape 3): no later candidate may be dominated by this counterexample.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: Agents, goods and values. Added to every solver.
fragments.text: % The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% A candidate: every good goes to one agent ...
1 { gets(A,G) : agent(A) } 1 :- good(G).
% ... and nobody envies anybody: A does not value B's bundle more than the own one.
:- agent(A), agent(B), A != B,
   #sum { V,G : gets(B,G), value(A,G,V) ; -V,G : gets(A,G), value(A,G,V) } > 0.
#show gets/2.

fragments.name: refine
fragments.description: Grounded once per counterexample: later candidates must not be dominated by it.
fragments.text:
#program refine(k).
% cex(k,alt(A,G)): in the k-th counterexample agent A gets good G.
% loses(k,A) / gains(k,A): agent A is worse / better off there than in the candidate.
loses(k,A) :- agent(A),
    #sum { V,G : cex(k,alt(A,G)), value(A,G,V) ; -V,G : gets(A,G), value(A,G,V) } < 0.
gains(k,A) :- agent(A),
    #sum { V,G : cex(k,alt(A,G)), value(A,G,V) ; -V,G : gets(A,G), value(A,G,V) } > 0.
% The candidate must not be dominated by it: if somebody gains, somebody loses.
:- gains(k,A), not loses(k,B) : agent(B).

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: who gets what.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for an allocation that Pareto-dominates the candidate (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: another allocation (it need not be envy-free) in which ...
1 { alt(A,G) : agent(A) } 1 :- good(G).
% ... nobody is worse off ...
:- agent(A), #sum { V,G : alt(A,G), value(A,G,V) ; -V,G : gets(A,G), value(A,G,V) } < 0.
% ... and somebody is better off.
gains(A) :- agent(A), #sum { V,G : alt(A,G), value(A,G,V) ; -V,G : gets(A,G), value(A,G,V) } > 0.
better :- gains(A).
:- not better.
#show alt/2.
% No relevant/1 rules: the loop passes the allocation alt/2 to the refine part.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction + refine
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.expand(refine, cex = X.atoms(alt/2))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

instances.facts:
% Three agents divide seven goods. value(A,G,V): good G is worth V to agent A;
% a bundle is worth the sum of its goods.
agent(1..3).
good(1..7).
value(1,1,1). value(1,2,2). value(1,3,2). value(1,4,6). value(1,5,3). value(1,6,5). value(1,7,5).
value(2,1,4). value(2,2,1). value(2,3,3). value(2,4,7). value(2,5,7). value(2,6,9). value(2,7,6).
value(3,1,9). value(3,2,8). value(3,3,9). value(3,4,5). value(3,5,1). value(3,6,1). value(3,7,6).

% Two agents who value three goods alike: whoever gets fewer goods envies the
% other, so no allocation is envy-free.
agent(1..2).
good(1..3).
value(A,G,1) :- agent(A), good(G).

% Two agents with opposite tastes over eight goods: each prefers the goods the other
% cares little about, and two goods (7, 8) both like.
agent(1..2).
good(1..8).
value(1,1,6). value(1,2,5). value(1,3,4). value(1,4,1). value(1,5,1). value(1,6,2). value(1,7,5). value(1,8,3).
value(2,1,1). value(2,2,2). value(2,3,1). value(2,4,6). value(2,5,5). value(2,6,4). value(2,7,5). value(2,8,3).

% Four agents divide eight goods.
agent(1..4).
good(1..8).
value(1,1,6). value(1,2,3). value(1,3,7). value(1,4,1). value(1,5,2). value(1,6,9). value(1,7,4). value(1,8,2).
value(2,1,2). value(2,2,6). value(2,3,1). value(2,4,9). value(2,5,4). value(2,6,1). value(2,7,3). value(2,8,5).
value(3,1,2). value(3,2,7). value(3,3,7). value(3,4,2). value(3,5,4). value(3,6,2). value(3,7,6). value(3,8,1).
value(4,1,9). value(4,2,7). value(4,3,1). value(4,4,2). value(4,5,4). value(4,6,1). value(4,7,2). value(4,8,6).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.block(M))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

solver A = shared + abstraction + refine
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Up to three dominating allocations per candidate, one rule each.
loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    L = C.models(assume G(M), limit 3)
    if L.size == 0:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))
    for X in L:
        A.expand(refine, cex = X.atoms(alt/2))

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# No relevant/1: the clause is lifted from the ground programs of both ends.
loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.lift(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

generators.name: additive
generators.description: Random additive values: every good is worth 1..m to every agent, uniformly and independently.
generators.text:
% additive: a agents, g goods, value(A,G,V) with V uniform in 1..m.
agent(1..a).
good(1..g).
value(A,G,@int(1, m, A, G)) :- agent(A), good(G).
#show agent/1.  #show good/1.  #show value/3.

library.summary: Envy-free and Pareto-efficient allocations of indivisible goods; a dominating allocation becomes a rule in the abstraction (Shape 3; 3 agents, 7 goods, 3 solutions).
